question: to the Commission Yannis Maniatis (S&D) Subject:

According to reports, despite the significant penetration of RES, Greece has only 0.22 GW of installed battery capacity (storage adequacy index – 2 % RES SAI), in contrast to neighbouring countries such as Bulgaria (3.5 GW / 52 % RES SAI). This year’s European Semester report for Greece acknowledges that increasing energy storage will reduce curtailments and increase the use of green electricity, and that Greece has made limited progress in implementing the 2025 recommendation (CSR) to develop flexibility solutions that include storage and contribute to making electricity prices more affordable. It also notes the significant and rapidly increasing curtailments and uncertainty, which are forcing smaller RES producers to exit the market. Finally, it calls on Greece to improve the design of support schemes with a view to adding smaller battery storage systems connected to RES installations. The Commission is asked: 1.
What are the Greek storage measures (investments and reforms) that were initially included in the Recovery Fund and have not yet been implemented?
How many MW of storage have been financed by the Recovery Fund and how many have been connected to the electricity system to date?
Can the annual cost to Greek energy prices from the delay in the implementation of projects be estimated?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (9.9.2026) Since its inception, the Greek Recovery and Resilience Plan (RRP) has included Measure 16926 (‘Support of the installation of storage systems to enhance renewable energy sources (RES) penetration’) which covers battery energy storage systems and the construction of a pumped hydro storage system in Amfilochia. The measure was revised due to objective circumstances, including the extended time needed for the electrification of the battery storage systems and supply bottlenecks affecting the timely delivery of equipment needed for the Amfilochia Pumped Hydro Storage facility. The final milestone 16 of Measure 16926 will be assessed as part of the ninth and final payment request that Greece is expected to submit in September 2026. The milestone requires: (i) the installation of battery energy storage projects with a total capacity of 700 megawatts (MW); and (ii) the completion of the civil engineering works for the Amfilochia Pumped Hydro Storage Station. The Commission has not carried out any analysis of the exact impact on electricity prices resulting from Greece’s lack of grid scale battery storage capacity. However, a lack of flexibility can generally contribute to greater price volatility and higher system costs. The factsheet1 published by the Commission in March 2026 provides additional information on how the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF) is supporting Greece’s transition away from polluting energy sources toward cleaner alternatives, such as wind and solar power.
